title: You're Not Watching the City. You're In It.
why: Nemesis story (the sealed party bus that calls transportation a tour) for groups who haven't picked yet; ends on the belief that the city is the show.
hook_options: Name one street you saw from the party bus.
Most group tours in New Orleans are just transportation with a speaker.
caption: Ask anyone who did the party bus to name one street they passed. They can't. They spent the ride behind tinted glass. We think New Orleans happens on the sidewalk: the brass band, the stranger who waves, the corner that cheers. Open air. Open city. #neworleans #nola #nolabachelorette #birthdayinnola

slides.headline: Name one street you saw from the party bus
Because you didn't see one
slides.body: Tinted windows. Rows of seats facing forward. An hour in traffic on Canal, and somebody calls it a tour.

slides.headline: The city happened without you
slides.body: A brass band played on the corner. A second line swung past. You heard a Bluetooth speaker.

slides.headline: So we took the windows off
slides.body: Open air. Your group faces each other across one long bar, not the back of a headrest.

slides.headline: The street becomes part of your group
slides.body: People on the sidewalk wave. They cheer. A few try to hop on. You're the thing they stop to watch.

slides.headline: A host, not a chauffeur
slides.body: Reads the group, cranks the music or slows down for the photo, makes the bride feel like the whole block is looking.

slides.headline: Photos with the actual city in them
slides.body: Not another bench seat in a dark van. The house, the oak, the corner, your people.

slides.headline: The city is the show
slides.body: We don't compete with the bars. We connect them, and make the in-between part the best part.

slides.headline: You're not watching New Orleans. You're in it.
Take the windows off your weekend
